# Jubilees Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Watchers; Nephilim; The Flood Decreed

---

**5:1** As the human population on the earth expanded and daughters were born, the angels of God looked down, saw how beautiful these women were, and took whichever ones they wanted as wives. These unions produced children — a race of giants.

**5:2** Wickedness exploded across the earth. Every living thing — humans, animals, birds, every creature — abandoned its proper way of living. They turned on each other and began destroying one another. Violence was everywhere, and every thought in every human mind was nothing but evil, all the time.

**5:3** God looked down at the earth. Everything was ruined. Every creature had abandoned its proper way. Everything on earth was doing every kind of evil imaginable before him.

**5:4** He declared that he would wipe out humanity and every living thing from the face of the earth he had made.

**5:5** But Noah found favor in the LORD's eyes.

**5:6** God was furious with the angels he had originally sent to earth. He commanded that they be stripped of all their authority and ordered us to chain them deep in the earth. That is where they remain — bound and confined.

**5:7** He was equally furious with their giant sons, who had been slaughtering each other with swords and drowning themselves in wickedness.

**5:8** So he unleashed war among the giants — each one killing his neighbor — until they had wiped each other out completely and not one was left on the earth.

**5:9** Their angelic fathers watched it happen. Then those angels were chained in the depths of the earth forever, held there until the day of the final condemnation — the day when everyone who corrupted their ways and deeds before the LORD faces justice.

**5:10** God destroyed every last one of them, and not a single creature escaped his judgment for what it had done.

**5:11** He then remade the nature of all his creatures — fresh and righteous — so that they would never again sin in their essential nature, but every kind of creature would always remain true to its own good design.

**5:12** Every judgment is fixed and recorded on the heavenly tablets in righteousness. That includes the judgment for anyone who strays from the path set out for them. Walk off that path — your judgment is already written, for every creature, every kind.

**5:13** Nothing escapes this record. Heaven, earth, light, darkness, the deepest abyss, the thickest shadow — every place of existence — everything is judged and everything is written on the heavenly tablets.

**5:14** Then God said: "My spirit will not remain in human beings forever. They are only flesh. I will limit their years to one hundred and twenty."

**5:15** He sent the sword among the giants, and they cut each other down until not one remained standing.

**5:16** Their fathers watched it happen, and then were themselves bound forever in the depths of the earth — held there until the day of the final judgment, when all who have corrupted their ways before God face the reckoning.

**5:17** God wiped out all their dwelling places. Not one of them escaped judgment for their wickedness.

**5:18** He created a new and righteous nature for all his living works, so that they would never again sin against their own design, and every creature would remain true to its kind forever.

**5:19** All judgment is set and recorded on the heavenly tablets in righteousness.

**5:20** With all this as the backdrop, Noah built the ark — in the twenty-seventh jubilee, fifth week, fifth year.

**5:21** He entered the ark in the sixth year. He sealed the doors on the seventeenth day of the second month, in the first year of the twenty-eighth jubilee. The LORD then opened seven floodgates in the sky and seven outlets in the great deep below.

**5:22** For forty days and forty nights, water poured down through those heavenly floodgates, while the deep pushed water up from below, until the entire world was submerged.

**5:23** The waters kept rising across the earth's surface, covering every mountain, until the water stood fifteen cubits above the highest peak.

**5:24** The ark lifted off the ground and floated across the face of the rising waters.

**5:25** The flood held the earth for five months — one hundred and fifty days.

**5:26** Then the ark came to rest on the summit of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat.

**5:27** In the fourth month the springs of the deep were sealed and the sky's floodgates were locked. On the first day of the seventh month, all the outlets of the earth's deep opened, and the water began draining back down.

**5:28** On the first day of the tenth month, the mountain peaks broke through the surface of the water. Noah was filled with joy.

**5:29** Forty days later Noah opened the ark's window and sent out a raven to check whether the flood had gone down. The raven came back — the ground was still covered everywhere.

**5:30** Noah waited seven more days and sent out a dove. It found nowhere to land and returned to him.

**5:31** Seven days after that, he sent the dove out again. This time it came back carrying an olive branch with fresh leaves in its beak. Noah knew: the earth was emerging.

**5:32** On the first day of the first month of the new year, Noah opened the roof of the ark. He looked out and saw dry land.

**5:33** During the twenty-eighth jubilee, Noah opened the ark and released all the animals, birds, cattle, and every living creature.

---
*PNEUMA notes: The doublet structure (vv.6-13 and 15-19) reflects a textual feature of the Ge'ez manuscript — likely parallel accounts; rendered sequentially as the text presents them. "Lubar" (v.26) kept as the Jubilees-specific Ararat peak name.*
